caption: $\pi/4$, numerically -- N(...) forces the fold plain evaluation withholds
Folds to $\pi/4$ exactly, as [[Arctan]] does at 1

sage.note: Ours takes arccot on (0, pi); Sage, SymPy and mpmath take (-pi/2, pi/2), so a negative argument has a negative value.
sympy.note: compute-engine's Arccot has range (0, pi), so a negative argument lands past pi/2 (arccot(-0.5) = 2.034); SymPy's acot takes (-pi/2, pi/2] and answers -1.107.
mpmath.note: compute-engine's Arccot has range (0, pi), so a negative argument lands past pi/2 (arccot(-0.5) = 2.034); mpmath's acot takes (-pi/2, pi/2] and answers -1.107.
julia.note: compute-engine's ArcCot has range (0, pi), so a negative argument lands past pi/2; the Julia mapping is atan(1/z), range (-pi/2, pi/2].
rust.note: Arccot is written as atan(1/x), with values in (-π/2, π/2); compute-engine's Arccot has range (0, π), so a negative x differs by π.

caption: $\operatorname{arccot} 0 = \pi/2$
rust.note: The mapping writes Arccot through the reciprocal 1/x, whose exact division by zero panics where compute-engine's value at 0 is defined (or a pole).

mpmath.note: mpmath's acot ranges over (-π/2, π/2], as Wolfram's ArcCot does, so acot(-1) is -π/4; compute-engine's Arccot ranges over (0, π).

julia.note: Nemo's balls have no infinite point, so an infinite operand can't be put to Julia; the call is not asked.
